close_reason: Fixed in e03d136: ChatMessageEntry.sender_id is now SenderId. Constructor signatures take SenderId directly (no impl Into<String>) to surface the variant choice at call sites. New test push_entry_self_sentinel_routes_to_owner covers "self" -> Owner deserialize routing.
description:
crate-jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs declares `ChatMessageEntry.sender_id: String` (line ~48). The wire shape is identical to `Message.sender_id` and `Reaction.sender_id` (both `SenderId` per message.rs:67) — same `"self"` sentinel, same `ChatContact.id` opaque-URI semantics, same draft section (§4.11 vs §5.2 in the push draft but both reference the same wire convention).

Diverging here means:
- A push-payload consumer reading `entry.sender_id` gets back a raw string and has to know to compare against `"self"` themselves to detect owner-sent messages. Every other type in the crate already gives them `SenderId::Owner` for that case.
- Pattern-matching code that handles owner-vs-contact has to be written twice with two different shapes.
- If the wire form ever evolves (e.g. spec adds a new sentinel for system-bot messages), updating `SenderId` covers the whole crate except this one struct.

JMAP-ly0n.4 already covers the same drift at `ChatTypingEvent.sender_id` (ephemeral.rs). This is the parallel third site. The fix is mechanical — replace `String` with `SenderId` — and `SenderId` already has the manual `Serialize` / `Deserialize` impls that round-trip exactly the same wire bytes, so the change is wire-compatible. Worth resolving in the same pass as JMAP-ly0n.4 rather than as a separate sweep, since the rationale and risk are identical.

(Note: the line-of-code itself appears to predate commit 9c0d34f and survived into the diff via doc-comment annotation only. The review scope "since 9c0d34f" captures the file as a whole, so the finding is in scope even though the field-declaration line was not added by this diff.)
title: ChatMessageEntry.sender_id in push.rs is String, not SenderId — parallel drift to JMAP-ly0n.4 in a different file
